ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB \parallel CD$, $AE$ and $CE$ bisect $\angle BAC$ and $\angle ACD$ respectively, $AE$ and $CE$ intersect at point $E$, draw line $ED \perp CD$ with the foot of the perpendicular being $D$, intersecting $AB$ at point $B$. If $AC=8, BD=6$, what is the area of $\triangle ACE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $EF\perp AC$ at point F from point E,\\
since $AB\parallel CD$ and $ED\perp CD$,\\
therefore $EB\perp AB$,\\
since $AE$ and $CE$ bisect $\angle BAC$ and $\angle ACD$ respectively,\\
therefore $BE=EF=ED$,\\
thus point E is the midpoint of $BD$,\\
since $AC=8$ and $BD=6$,\\
therefore $EF=\frac{1}{2}BD=3$,\\
thus, the area of $\triangle ACE$ is $\frac{1}{2}\times AC\times EF=\frac{1}{2}\times 8\times 3=\boxed{12}$
